blocks.text: Many plant cells are totipotent: a single cell can form a new plant, so biologists can grow a whole plant from one transgenic cell. The main purposes of transgenic plants are:

items: Insect resistance: genes of Bacillus thuringiensis, a soil bacterium, have been put into many plants (cotton, rice, maize, potato, tomato, brinjal, cauliflower, cabbage and others); they make proteins that kill insect pests but do not harm useful insects.
Herbicide resistance: many crops have been made resistant to glyphosate, a herbicide.

Better nutrition: transgenic 'golden rice' for areas short of dietary iron and vitamin A. Genes from beans, the fungus Aspergillus and wild rice were added to raise iron content, and genes for beta-carotene (the precursor of vitamin A) from daffodil.
Biopharmaceuticals: GMO plants and plant cells make cytokines, hormones, antibodies, enzymes and vaccines.

blocks.alt: A cycle. Bacillus thuringiensis gives the gene of Bacillus thuringiensis, which is put into a maize plant. An insect pest feeds on the leaves; proteins made by the plant kill the insect pest (a curled, dead caterpillar). The result is a transgenic plant.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: Each year iron deficiency affects 1.4 billion women, and vitamin A deficiency kills 670,000 children and causes 500,000 cases of irreversible childhood blindness.
